title: Sri Rama pattabhishekam
introduction: At the request of Bharata to take back the kingdom of Ayodhya, Rama accepts the offer and sits on a seat. Bharata and Rama take their bath and get adorned for the occasion. Rama, mounting on an excellent chariot, sallies forth on a procession in the city accompanied by Bharata, Shatrughna, Lakshmana and Vibhishana. Nine thousand elephants follow the procession, with Sugreeva and other monkeys mounted on them. Some attendants and musicians with their musical instruments walk in front of Rama's procession. The citizens of Ayodhya host flags on every house. Rama returns to his paternal palace in Ayodhya. Sugreeva orders four of his monkeys to bring water from four oceans in jars given to them. Some monkeys brought water from five hundred rivers, as also from the four oceans for the purpose of the ceremony. Vasishta along with other brahmins as priests caused Rama to be consecrated with that water. The virgins, ministers, warriors, merchants, the four gods as well as other gods sprinkled sap of all kinds of herbs on Rama. Vasishta and other priests officiating the coronation-ceremony adorned Rama with an auspicious and charming crown. Then, Rama gives away presents to the priests as well as Sugreeva and Angada. Rama presents a pearl-necklace to Seetha and Seetha presents that necklace in turn to Hanuma. Rama further gives away presents to Vibhishana, Sugreeva, Jambavan and others on the occasion. Rama bids farewell to monkeys. The glory of the epic is complemented in the end by Valmiki.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे अष्टाविंशत्यधिक शततमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 128th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
शिरस्यञ्जलिमादाय कैकेयीनन्दिवर्धनः |
बभाषे भरतो ज्येष्ठन् रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्
verses.iast:
śirasyañjalimAdAya kaikeyInandivardhanaḥ |
babhAṣe bharato jyeṣṭhan rAmaṃ satyaparAkramam
verses.translation: Placing his hallowed hands together on his head (as a mark of salutation), Bharata the enhancer of Kaikeyi's happiness, spoke to the truly brave Rama, his elder brother (as follows):

glosses.meaning: his open hands placed side by side together and slightly hallowed
on his head (as a token of salutation).

verses.devanagari:
पूजिता मामिका माता दत्तन् राज्यमिदं मम |
तद्ददामि पुनस्तुभ्यन् यथा त्वमददा मम
verses.iast:
pUjitA mAmikA mAtA dattan rAjyamidaṃ mama |
taddadAmi punastubhyan yathA tvamadadA mama
verses.translation: "You gave this kingdom to me and treated my mother's words respectfully. As you gave it to me then, in the same way I am giving it to you again.

verses.devanagari:
धुरमेकाकिना न्यस्तामृषभेण बलीयसा |
किशोरवद्गुरुं भारं न वोढुमहमुत्सहे
verses.iast:
dhuramekAkinA nyastAmṛṣabheṇa balIyasA |
kiśoravadguruṃ bhAraṃ na voḍhumahamutsahe
verses.translation: I cannot carry this heavy burden anymore than a young ox would sustain a load, carried forward by a strong bull all alone."

verses.devanagari:
वारिवेगेन महता भिन्नः सेतुरिव क्षरन् |
दुर्बन्धनमिदं मन्ये राज्यच्छिद्रमसन्वृतम्
verses.iast:
vArivegena mahatA bhinnaḥ seturiva kṣaran |
durbandhanamidaṃ manye rAjyacchidramasanvṛtam
verses.translation: "I think this venerable point in the form of administration of the kingdom is difficult to be controlled, as a broken dam, seeping from its cracks when breached mammoth stream of water.

glosses.meaning: weak point in administration of the kingdom
vaasivegena = (when breached) by a mammoth stream of water.

verses.devanagari:
गतिं खर इवाश्वस्य हन्सस्येव च वायसः |
नान्वेतुमुत्सहे देव तव मार्गमरिन्दम
verses.iast:
gatiṃ khara ivAśvasya hansasyeva ca vAyasaḥ |
nAnvetumutsahe deva tava mArgamarindama
verses.translation: O hero, the annihilator of enemies! I am not able to follow your path, any more than a donkey would follow the gallop of a horse or a crow would take up the chase of a wild goose."

verses.devanagari:
यथा च रोपितो वृक्षो जातश्चान्तर्निवेशने |
महांश्च सुदुरारोहो महास्कन्धः प्रशाखवान्
शीर्येत पुष्पितो भूत्वा न फलानि प्रदर्शयेत् |
तस्य नानुभवेदर्थन् यस्य हेतोः स रोप्यते
एषोपमा महाबाहो त्वमर्थन् वेत्तुमर्हसि |
यद्यस्मान्मनुजेन्द्र त्वं भक्तान्भृत्यान्न शाधि हि
verses.iast:
yathA ca ropito vṛkṣo jAtaścAntarniveśane |
mahAṃśca sudurAroho mahAskandhaḥ praśAkhavAn
śIryeta puṣpito bhUtvA na phalAni pradarśayet |
tasya nAnubhavedarthan yasya hetoḥ sa ropyate
eṣopamA mahAbAho tvamarthan vettumarhasi |
yadyasmAnmanujendra tvaṃ bhaktAnbhṛtyAnna śAdhi hi
verses.translation: "O mighty armed king! How a tree planted in the back yard of one's own house, even though grown big and difficult to climb with a huge trunk and large branches, does not yield fruits but dries up after flowering, he who planted it would not enjoy the fruit for which it was planted. This is the analogy applied to you, if you, as a Master, would not indeed rule over us, your servants. You can understand the meaning."

glosses.meaning: in the black-yard of one's own house
would not indeed rule over us

verses.devanagari:
जगदद्याभिषिक्तन् त्वामनुपश्यतु सर्वतः |
प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं मध्याह्ने दीप्ततेजसं
verses.iast:
jagadadyAbhiṣiktan tvAmanupaśyatu sarvataḥ |
pratapantamivAdityaṃ madhyAhne dIptatejasaṃ
verses.translation: "O Rama! Today, let the world see you when crowned, like the sun with its glowing splendour, shining brilliantly at noon.

verses.devanagari:
तूर्यसङ्घातनिर्घोषैः काञ्चीनूपुरनिस्वनैः |
मधुरैर्गीतशब्दैश्च प्रतिबुध्यस्व शेष्व च
verses.iast:
tUryasañghAtanirghoṣaiḥ kAñcInUpuranisvanaiḥ |
madhurairgItaśabdaiśca pratibudhyasva śeṣva ca
verses.translation: May you relax and wake-up too, to the sounds of an ensemble of musical instruments, the tinkling of ornaments strung with tiny bells and worn around the waist and anklets as well as sweet invocation of songs.

glosses.meaning: to the sounds of an ensemble of musical instruments
noise of ornaments strung with tiny bells and worn around the waist and anklets

verses.devanagari:
यावदावर्तते चक्रन् यावती च वसुन्धरा |
तावत्त्वमिह सर्वस्य स्वामित्वमभिवर्तय
verses.iast:
yAvadAvartate cakran yAvatI ca vasundharA |
tAvattvamiha sarvasya svAmitvamabhivartaya
verses.translation: Look after, you, lordship of world here, as long as the stellar sphere revolves and so far as the earth is spread out."

verses.devanagari:
भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रामः परपुरञ्जयः |
तथेति प्रतिजग्राह निषसादासने शुभे
verses.iast:
bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvA rAmaḥ parapurañjayaḥ |
tatheti pratijagrAha niṣasAdAsane śubhe
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Bharata, Rama who conquered the cities of adversaries, accepted his words saying "Be it so" and sat on an auspicious seat.

glosses.meaning: who conquered the cities of adversaries

verses.devanagari:
ततः शत्रुघ्नवचनान्निपुणाः श्मश्रुवर्धकाः |
सुखहस्ताः सुशीघ्राश्च राघवं पर्युपासत
verses.iast:
tataḥ śatrughnavacanAnnipuṇAḥ śmaśruvardhakAḥ |
sukhahastAḥ suśIghrAśca rAghavaṃ paryupAsata
verses.translation: Thereafter, on instructions from Shatrughna, skilled barbers with gentle hands who can do their work with a good speed, encircled Rama all round.

glosses.meaning: who can do with a good speed

verses.devanagari:
पूर्वन् तु भरते स्नाते लक्ष्मणे च महाबले |
सुग्रीवे वानरेन्द्रे च राक्षसेन्द्रे विभीषणे
विशोधितजटः स्नातश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः |
महार्हवसनोपेतस्तस्थौ तत्र श्रिया ज्वलन्
verses.iast:
pUrvan tu bharate snAte lakṣmaṇe ca mahAbale |
sugrIve vAnarendre ca rAkṣasendre vibhIṣaṇe
viśodhitajaṭaḥ snAtaścitramAlyAnulepanaḥ |
mahArhavasanopetastasthau tatra śriyA jvalan
verses.translation: Bharata, having bathed first, the mighty Lakshmana, Sugreeva the lord of monkeys and Vibhishana the king of demons took bath. Rama had his matted locks disentangled and bathed. He stood there, shining with splendour, adorned with picturesque garlands, smeared with sandal pastes of various colours and clothed in costly raiment.

glosses.meaning: adorned with picturesque garlands and smeared with sandal pastes of various colours

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिकर्म च रामस्य कारयामास वीर्यवान् |
लक्ष्मणस्य च लक्ष्मीवानिक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्धनः
verses.iast:
pratikarma ca rAmasya kArayAmAsa vIryavAn |
lakṣmaṇasya ca lakṣmIvAnikṣvAkukulavardhanaḥ
verses.translation: Shatrughna, the valiant and charming man, the promoter of Ikshvaku dynasty made arrangements for personal adornment of Rama and Lakshmana.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिकर्म च सीतायाः सर्वा दशरथस्त्रियः |
आत्मनैव तदा चक्रुर्मनस्विन्यो मनोहरम्
verses.iast:
pratikarma ca sItAyAḥ sarvA daśarathastriyaḥ |
Atmanaiva tadA cakrurmanasvinyo manoharam
verses.translation: Then, all the noble-minded widows of Dasaratha indeed themselves personally adorned Seetha beautifully.

verses.devanagari:
ततो राघवपत्नीनान् सर्वासामेव शोभनम् |
चकार यत्नात्कौसल्या प्रहृष्टा पुत्रवत्सला
verses.iast:
tato rAghavapatnInAn sarvAsAmeva śobhanam |
cakAra yatnAtkausalyA prahṛṣṭA putravatsalA
verses.translation: Thereupon, the delightful Kausalya, who was affectionate of her sons, adorned with zeal all the wives of monkeys.

glosses.meaning: who was affectionate of her sons

verses.devanagari:
ततः शत्रुघ्नवचनात्सुमन्त्रो नाम सारथिः |
योजयित्वाभिचक्राम रथन् सर्वाङ्गशोभनम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ śatrughnavacanAtsumantro nAma sArathiḥ |
yojayitvAbhicakrAma rathan sarvAñgaśobhanam
verses.translation: Later, on the orders of Shatrughna, the charioteer by name Sumantra made his appearance, yoking chariot to horses which were completely beautiful in all respects.

verses.devanagari:
अर्कमण्डलसङ्काशन् दिव्यं दृष्ट्वा रथन् स्थितम् |
आरुरोह महाबाहू रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
verses.iast:
arkamaṇḍalasañkAśan divyaṃ dṛṣṭvA rathan sthitam |
Aruroha mahAbAhU rAmaḥ satyaparAkramaḥ
verses.translation: Seeing the charming chariot, which emitted immaculate splendour like that of the sun, standing before him, the mighty armed Rama, the conqueror of hostile cities, ascended it.

glosses.meaning: which emitted immaculate splendor like that of the sun

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवो हनुमांश्चैव महेन्द्रसदृशद्युती |
स्नातौ दिव्यनिभैर्वस्त्रैर्जग्मतुः शुभकुण्डलौ
verses.iast:
sugrīvo hanumāṃścaiva mahendrasadṛśadyutī |
snātau divyanibhairvastrairjagmatuḥ śubhakuṇḍalau
verses.translation: Sugreeva and Hanuma, having splendour similar to that of Indra the lord of celestials, after taking their bat, wore beautiful raiment as well as sparkling ear rings and started.

glosses.meaning: having a splendor similar to that of Indra the lord of celestials

verses.devanagari:
सर्वाभरणजुष्टाश्च ययुस्ताः शुभकुण्डलाः |
सुग्रीवपत्न्याः सीता च द्रष्टुं नगरमुत्सुकाः
verses.iast:
sarvābharaṇajuṣṭāśca yayustāḥ śubhakuṇḍalāḥ |
sugrīvapatnyāḥ sītā ca draṣṭuṃ nagaramutsukāḥ
verses.translation: Endowed with all types of ornaments as well as charming ear-rings, those wives of Sugreeva together with Seetha moved out, longing as they were, to see the city.

glosses.meaning: endowed with all types of ornaments

verses.devanagari:
अयोध्यायान् तु सचिवा राज्ञो दशरथस्य च |
पुरोहितं पुरस्कृत्य मन्त्रयामासुरर्थवत्
verses.iast:
ayodhyAyAn tu sacivA rAGYo daśarathasya ca |
purohitaṃ puraskṛtya mantrayAmAsurarthavat
verses.translation: In Ayodhya, the ministers of king Dasaratha, having placed the priest in their front, planned everything meaningfully.

glosses.meaning: having placed the priest in their front

verses.devanagari:
अशोको विजयश्चैव सिद्धार्थश्च समाहिताः |
मन्त्रयन्रामवृद्ध्यर्थन् वृत्त्यर्थं नगरस्य च
verses.iast:
aśoko vijayaścaiva siddhārthaśca samāhitāḥ |
mantrayanrAmavṛddhyarthan vṛttyarthaṃ nagarasya ca
verses.translation: Ashoka, Vijaya and Siddhartha, with a great concern, discussed about Rama's advancement and the prosperity of the City.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वमेवाभिषेकार्थन् जयार्हस्य महात्मनः |
कर्तुमर्हथ रामस्य यद्यन्मङ्गलपूर्वकम्
verses.iast:
sarvamevAbhiṣekArthan jayArhasya mahAtmanaḥ |
kartumarhatha rAmasya yadyanmañgalapUrvakam
verses.translation: "You ought to do auspiciously whatever is required for the coronation of the great-souled Rama, worthy of victory."

verses.devanagari:
इति ते मन्त्रिणः सर्वे सन्दिश्य तु पुरोहितम्
नगरान्निर्ययुस्तूर्णन् रामदर्शनबुद्धयः
verses.iast:
iti te mantriṇaḥ sarve sandiśya tu purohitam
nagarAnniryayustUrṇan rAmadarśanabuddhayaḥ
verses.translation: Advising the priest in this way, all those ministers quickly started from the city, with an intention to see Rama.

glosses.meaning: with an intention to see Rama.

verses.devanagari:
हरियुक्तन् सहस्राक्षो रथमिन्द्र इवानघः |
प्रययौ रथमास्थाय रामो नगरमुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
hariyuktan sahasrAkṣo rathamindra ivAnaghaḥ |
prayayau rathamAsthAya rAmo nagaramuttamam
verses.translation: The faultless Rama, mounting the excellent chariot, as Indra ascended the chariot yoked to green-coloured horses, sallied forth to the city.

glosses.meaning: indraH iva = as the thousand-eyed Indra

verses.devanagari:
जग्राह भरतो रश्मीञ्शत्रुघ्नश्छत्रमाददे |
लक्ष्मणो व्यजनन् तस्य मूर्ध्नि सम्पर्यवीजयत्
श्वेतन् च वालव्यजनन् सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः |
अपरन् चन्द्रसङ्काशन् राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः
verses.iast:
jagrAha bharato raśmIñśatrughnaśchatramAdade |
lakṣmaṇo vyajanan tasya mUrdhni samparyavIjayat
śvetan ca vAlavyajanan sugrIvo vAnareśvaraḥ |
aparan candrasañkAśan rAkṣasendro vibhIṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Bharata took up the reins. Shatrughna held the parasol on Rama's head. Lakshmana winnowed a fan. Vibhishana, the king of demons standing nearby, held a white fan, shining brilliantly like the moon.

verses.devanagari:
ऋषिसङ्घैर्तदाकाशे देवैश्च समरुद्गणैः |
स्तूयमानस्य रामस्य शुश्रुवे मधुरध्वनिः
verses.iast:
ṛṣisañghairtadAkAśe devaiśca samarudgaṇaiḥ |
stUyamAnasya rAmasya śuśruve madhuradhvaniḥ
verses.translation: Then, in the sky, groups of sages, celestials along with troop of the Maruts, the host of the gods, praised Rama and sweet reverberation was heard.

glosses.meaning: along with troop of the Maruts

verses.devanagari:
ततः शत्रुञ्जयं नाम कुञ्जरं पर्वतोपमम् |
आरुरोह महातेजाः सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः
verses.iast:
tataḥ śatruñjayaṃ nAma kuñjaraṃ parvatopamam |
Aruroha mahAtejAḥ sugrIvo vAnareśvaraḥ
verses.translation: Thereupon, Sugreeva, the foremost of monkeys, possessing a great splendor, mounted an elephant named Shatrunjaya, looking like a mountain.

verses.devanagari:
नवनागसहस्राणि ययुरास्थाय वानराः |
मानुषन् विग्रहन् कृत्वा सर्वाभरणभूषिताः
verses.iast:
navanAgasahasrAṇi yayurAsthAya vAnarAḥ |
mAnuṣan vigrahan kṛtvA sarvAbharaṇabhUṣitAḥ
verses.translation: Assuming human forms and adorned with all types of ornaments, monkeys sallied forth, mounting on mine thousand elephants.

glosses.meaning: and adorned with all types of ornaments

verses.devanagari:
शङ्खशब्दप्रणादैश्च दुन्दुभीनान् च निस्वनैः |
प्रययू पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तां पुरीन् हर्म्यमालिनीम्
verses.iast:
śañkhaśabdapraṇAdaiśca dundubhInAn ca nisvanaiḥ |
prayayU puruṣavyAghrastAṃ purIn harmyamAlinIm
verses.translation: Rama, the foremost among men, accompanied by sounds of conches buzzing in the ears and sounds of kettle-drums, proceeded to the city of Ayodhya, having a series of palaces.

glosses.meaning: with sounds of couches among men buzzing in the ear

verses.devanagari:
ददृशुस्ते समायान्तन् राघवं सपुरःसरम् |
विराजमानन् वपुषा रथेनातिरथन् तदा
verses.iast:
dadṛśuste samAyAntan rAghavaṃ sapuraḥsaram |
virAjamAnan vapuṣA rathenAtirathan tadA
verses.translation: Then, the people of Ayodhya saw Rama, the chariot warrior, having a beautiful form, arriving on a chariot, with attendants walking in front.

verses.devanagari:
ते वर्धयित्वा काकुत्स्थन् रामेण प्रतिनन्दिताः |
अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं भ्रातृभिः परिवारितम्
verses.iast:
te vardhayitvA kAkutsthan rAmeṇa pratinanditAḥ |
anujagmurmahAtmAnaṃ bhrAtṛbhiḥ parivAritam
verses.translation: Felicitating Rama and greeted in reciprocation by Rama, they followed the great souled Rama, who was surrounded by his brothers.

verses.devanagari:
अमात्यैर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैव तथा प्रकृतिभिर्वृतः |
श्रिया विरुरुचे रामो नक्षत्रैरिव चन्द्रमाः
verses.iast:
amAtyairbrAhmaṇaiścaiva tathA prakṛtibhirvṛtaḥ |
śriyA viruruce rAmo nakṣatrairiva candramAḥ
verses.translation: Surrounded by ministers, brahamanas and other citizens, Rama shone with his own brilliance, like the moon among the stars.

verses.devanagari:
स पुरोगामिभिस्तूर्यैस्तालस्वस्तिकपाणिभिः |
प्रव्याहरद्भिर्मुदितैर्मङ्गलानि ययौ वृतः
verses.iast:
sa purogAmibhistUryaistAlasvastikapAṇibhiḥ |
pravyAharadbhirmuditairmañgalAni yayau vṛtaḥ
verses.translation: That Rama drove, surrounded by musicians having musical instruments cymbals and Swastika-musical instruments in their hands walking in front and uttering auspicious songs.

glosses.meaning: cymbals and swastika-instruments of music in their hands

verses.devanagari:
अक्षतन् जातरूपं च गावः कन्यास्तथा द्विजाः |
नरा मोदकहस्ताश्च रामस्य पुरतो ययुः
verses.iast:
akṣatan jAtarUpaṃ ca gAvaḥ kanyAstathA dvijAḥ |
narA modakahastAśca rAmasya purato yayuḥ
verses.translation: Men with grains of rice mixed with turmeric and thereby appearing gold in colour, cows, maidens along with brahmanas having balls of sweets in their hands, walked in front of Rama.

glosses.meaning: having balls of sweets in their hands

verses.devanagari:
सख्यन् च रामः सुग्रीवे प्रभावं चानिलात्मजे |
वानराणान् च तत्कर्म व्याचचक्षेअथ मन्त्रिणाम्
verses.iast:
sakhyan ca rAmaḥ sugrIve prabhAvaṃ cAnilAtmaje |
vAnarAṇAn ca tatkarma vyAcacakṣeatha mantriṇAm
verses.translation: Then, Rama narrated about his friendship established with Sugreeva, the power of Hanuma and the great act of monkeys to his ministers.

glosses.meaning: about his friendship established with Sugreeva

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा च विस्मयन् जग्मुरयोध्यापुरवासिनः |
वानराणां च तत्कर्म राक्षसानां च तद्बलम्
verses.iast:
śrutvA ca vismayan jagmurayodhyApuravAsinaḥ |
vānarāṇāṃ ca tatkarma rākṣasānāṃ ca tadbalam
verses.translation: Hearing the well-known achievement monkeys and the commonly known strength of the demons, the citizens of Ayodhya were astonished.

verses.devanagari:
विभीषणस्य संयोगमाचचक्षेऽथ मन्त्रिणाम् |
द्युतिमानेतदाख्याय रामो वानरसन्वृतः
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णामयोध्यां प्रविवेश ह |
verses.iast:
vibhīṣaṇasya saṃyogamācacakṣe'tha mantriṇām |
dyutimAnetadAkhyAya rAmo vAnarasanvṛtaḥ
hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanAkIrṇAmayodhyAṃ praviveśa ha |
verses.translation: Then, Rama spoke to his counselors about his meeting with Vibhishana. After recounting it, the resplendent Rama entered Ayodhya crowded with happy and rejoiced people, together with the monkeys.

glosses.meaning: crowded with rejoiced and happy people

verses.devanagari:
ततो ह्यभ्युच्छ्रयन्पौराः पताकास्ते गृहे गृहे
ऐक्ष्वाकाध्युषितन् रम्यमाससाद पितुर्गृहम् |
verses.iast:
tato hyabhyucchrayanpaurAḥ patAkAste gṛhe gṛhe
aikṣvAkAdhyuṣitan ramyamAsasAda piturgṛham |
verses.translation: Then, the citizens hoisted flags on every house. Rama reached the beautiful palace, paternal occupied by Ikshvaku kings.

verses.devanagari:
अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रो भरतं धर्मिणां वरम्
अर्थोपहितया वाचा मधुरं रघुनन्दनः |
पितुर्भवनमासाद्य प्रविश्य च महात्मनः
कौसल्यान् च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत् |
verses.iast:
athābravīdrājaputro bharataṃ dharmiṇāṃ varam
arthopahitayā vācā madhuraṃ raghunandanaḥ |
piturbhavanamAsAdya praviśya ca mahAtmanaḥ
kausalyAn ca sumitrAṃ ca kaikeyIṃ cAbhyavAdayat |
verses.translation: Approaching and entering the palace of the great-souled father, Rama the prince offered salutation to Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi and spoke the following sweet and meaningful words to Bharata, the foremost among the righteous:

verses.devanagari:
तच्च मद्भवनन् श्रेष्ठं साशोकवनिकं महत्
मुक्तावैदूर्यसङ्कीर्णन् सुग्रीवस्य निवेदय |
verses.iast:
tacca madbhavanan śreṣṭhaṃ sAśokavanikaṃ mahat
muktAvaidUryasañkIrṇan sugrIvasya nivedaya |
verses.translation: "Give this great palace of mine which looks excellent with Ashoka garden and consisting of pearls and cat's eye-gems to Sugreeva for his stay."

glosses.meaning: and consisting of pearls and cat's eye gems

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनन् श्रुत्वा भरतः सत्यविक्रमः
हस्ते गृहीत्वा सुग्रीवं प्रविवेश तमालयम् |
verses.iast:
tasya tadvacanan śrutvA bharataḥ satyavikramaḥ
haste gṛhītvā sugrīvaṃ praviveśa tamālayam |
verses.translation: Hearing those words of Rama, Bharata having a true prowess, holding Sugreeva by his hand, entered that house.

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तैलप्रदीपांश्च पर्यङ्कास्तरणानि च
गृहीत्वा विविशुः क्षिप्रं शत्रुघ्नेन प्रचोदिताः |
verses.iast:
tatastailapradīpāṃśca paryaṇ^kāstaraṇāni ca
gṛhītvā viviśuḥ kṣipraṃ śatrughnena pracoditāḥ |
verses.translation: Thereupon, some men as ordered by Shatrughna, quickly brought oil lamps, beds as also mats and entered the house.

verses.devanagari:
उवाच च महातेजाः सुग्रीवन् राघवानुजः
अभिषेकाय रामस्य दूतानाज्ञापय प्रभो |
verses.iast:
uvAca ca mahAtejAḥ sugrIvan rAghavAnujaḥ
abhiṣekAya rAmasya dUtAnAGYApaya prabho |
verses.translation: Bharata of great splendour spoke to Sugreeva as follows: "O capable person! Order the messengers to make arrangements for Rama's coronation."

verses.devanagari:
सौवर्णान्वानरेन्द्राणान् चतुर्णां चतुरो घटान्
ददौ क्षिप्रन् स सुग्रीवः सर्वरत्नविभूषितान् |
verses.iast:
sauvarṇAnvAnarendrAṇAn caturṇAṃ caturo ghaṭAn
dadau kṣipran sa sugrIvaḥ sarvaratnavibhUṣitAn |
verses.translation: Sugreeva then gave four golden jars encrusted with jewels, to four leaders of monkeys.

verses.devanagari:
यथा प्रत्यूषसमये चतुर्णान् सागराम्भसाम्
पूर्णैर्घटैः प्रतीक्षध्वन् तथा कुरुत वानराः |
verses.iast:
yathA pratyUṣasamaye caturṇAn sAgarAmbhasAm
pUrṇairghaṭaiḥ pratIkṣadhvan tathA kuruta vAnarAḥ |
verses.translation: "O monkeys! Get ready in such a way that you await my orders tomorrow at dawn, with your water-jars filled with water from the four oceans respectively."

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ता महात्मानो वानरा वारणोपमाः
उत्पेतुर्गगनन् शीघ्रन् गरुडा इव शीघ्रगाः |
verses.iast:
evamuktA mahAtmAno vAnarA vAraṇopamAḥ
utpeturgaganan śIghran garuḍA iva śIghragAḥ |
verses.translation: The great souled monkeys, resembling elephants and going speedily like eagles, thus ordered by Sugreeva, leapt quickly into the sky.

verses.devanagari:
जाम्बवांश्च हनूमांश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः
ऋषभश्चैव कलशाञ्जलपूर्णानथानयन् |
नदीशतानां पञ्चानान् जले कुम्भैरुपाहरन्
verses.iast:
jAmbavAṃśca hanUmAṃśca vegadarśI ca vAnaraḥ
ṛṣabhaścaiva kalaśAñjalapUrṇAnathAnayan |
nadIśatAnAṃ pañcAnAn jale kumbhairupAharan
verses.translation: Jambavan, Hanuma, a monkey called Vegadarshi and Rishabha brought water-jars filled with water. They brought water from five hundred rivers with those jars.

glosses.meaning: from five hundred rivers kumbhaiH = with (those) jars.

verses.devanagari:
पूर्वात्समुद्रात्कलशन् जलपूर्णमथानयत् |
सुषेणः सत्त्वसम्पन्नः सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्
verses.iast:
pUrvAtsamudrAtkalaśan jalapUrṇamathAnayat |
suṣeṇaḥ sattvasampannaḥ sarvaratnavibhUṣitam
verses.translation: Thereafter, the energetic SusheNa brought a jar, adorned with all types of precious stones, filled with water from the eastern sea.

glosses.meaning: and adorned with all types of precious stones.

verses.devanagari:
ऋषभो दक्षिणात्तूर्णन् समुद्राज्जलमाहरत् |
रक्तचन्दनकर्पूरैः सन्वृतन् काञ्चनं घटम्
verses.iast:
ṛṣabho dakṣiṇAttUrṇan samudrAjjalamAharat |
raktacandanakarpUraiḥ sanvṛtan kAñcanaṃ ghaṭam
verses.translation: Rishabha brought water quickly from the southern sea in a golden jar, covered with some stems of red sandal-wood tree.

verses.devanagari:
गवयः पश्चिमात्तोयमाजहार महार्णवात् |
रत्नकुम्भेन महता शीतं मारुतविक्रमः
verses.iast:
gavayaḥ paścimAttoyamAjahAra mahArṇavAt |
ratnakumbhena mahatA śItaṃ mArutavikramaḥ
verses.translation: Gavaya, having a pace as rapid as wind, brought cool water from the western ocean, in a large jar set with jewels.

glosses.meaning: having a pace rapid as wind
in a large jar set with jewels.

verses.devanagari:
उत्तराच्च जलन् शीघ्रन् गरुडानिलविक्रमः |
आजहार स धर्मात्मा नलः सर्वगुणान्वितः
verses.iast:
uttarAcca jalan śIghran garuḍAnilavikramaḥ |
ājahāra sa dharmātmā nalaḥ sarvaguṇānvitaḥ
verses.translation: That virtuous Nala, who vied with Garuda (the king of birds) and the wind-god in prowess, and who was endowed with all good qualities, swiftly brought water form the northern sea.

glosses.meaning: who vied with Garuda (the king of birds) and the wind-god in prowess
and who was endowed with all good qualities

verses.devanagari:
ततसैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरानीतं प्रेक्ष्य तज्जलम् |
अभिषेकाय रामस्य शत्रुघ्नः सचिवैः सह
पुरोहिताय श्रेष्ठाय सुहृद्भ्यश् च न्यवेदयत् |
verses.iast:
tatasairvānaraśreṣṭhairānītaṃ prekṣya tajjalam |
abhiṣekAya rAmasya śatrughnaḥ sacivaiḥ saha
purohitAya śreṣṭhAya suhṛdbhyaś ca nyavedayat |
verses.translation: Then, Shatrughna, accompanied by the counsellors, reported to Vasishta, their chief priest and his friends, about that water intended for Rama's coronation brought by those foremost of monkeys.

verses.devanagari:
ततः स प्रयतो वृद्धो वसिष्ठो ब्राह्मणैः सह
रामन् रत्नमयो पीठे सहसीतं न्यवेशयत् |
verses.iast:
tataḥ sa prayato vṛddho vasiṣṭho brAhmaṇaiḥ saha
rAman ratnamayo pIṭhe sahasItaṃ nyaveśayat |
verses.translation: The elderly Vasistha, with diligence, along with other brahmins on his side, prevailed upon Rama duly to occupy along with Seetha, on a seat made of precious stones.

glosses.meaning: along with other Brahmins at his side
prevailed upon Rama duly to occupy

verses.devanagari:
वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिरथ काश्यपः
कात्यायनः सुयज्ञश्च गौतमो विजयस्तथा |
अभ्यषिञ्चन्नरव्याघ्रं प्रसन्नेन सुगन्धिना
सलिलेन सहस्राक्षन् वसवो वासवं यथा |
verses.iast:
vasiṣṭho vAmadevaśca jAbAliratha kAśyapaḥ
kAtyAyanaḥ suyaGYaśca gautamo vijayastathA |
abhyaṣiñcannaravyAghraṃ prasannena sugandhinA
salilena sahasrAkṣan vasavo vAsavaṃ yathA |
verses.translation: Vasishta, Vamadeva, Kashyapa, Katyayana, Suyajna, Gautama and Vijaya consecrated Rama the tiger among men, with clear and fragrant water, as the eight Vasus*
notes: * Eight Vasus: 1. Aapa (connected with water), 2. Dhruva the pole-star, 3. Soma the moon, 4. Dhara, 5. Anila, the wind, 6. Pavaka the fire, 7. Pratyusha, the Dawn , 8. Prabhasa the Light.

verses.devanagari:
ऋत्विग्भिर्ब्राह्मणैः पूर्वन् कन्याभिर्मन्त्रिभिस्तथा
योधैश्चैवाभ्यषिञ्चन्स्ते सम्प्रहृष्टाः सनैगमैः |
सर्वौषधिरसैश्चापि दैवतैर्नभसि स्थितैः
चतुर्हिर्लोकपालैश्च सर्वैर्देवैश्च सङ्गतैः |
verses.iast:
ṛtvigbhirbrAhmaṇaiḥ pUrvan kanyAbhirmantribhistathA
yodhaiścaivAbhyaṣiñcanste samprahṛṣṭAḥ sanaigamaiḥ |
sarvauṣadhirasaiścApi daivatairnabhasi sthitaiḥ
caturhirlokapAlaiśca sarvairdevaiśca sañgataiḥ |
verses.translation: Vasishta and others, with much delight got him consecrated first, with brahmanas officiating as priests and by virgins, ministers, warriors, as well as merchants sprinkling the sap of all kinds of medicinal herbs, with the four gods the guardians of the worlds, standing in the air and with all the gods assembled there, sprinkling the sap on Rama.

glosses.meaning: and of all kinds of medicinal herbs

verses.devanagari:
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं पूर्वं किरीटं रत्नशोभितम्
अभिषिक्तः पुरा येन मनुस्तं दीप्ततेजसम् |
तस्यान्ववाये राजानः क्रमाद्येनाभिषेचिताः
सभायां हेमक्लुप्तायां शोभितायां महाधनैः |
रत्नैर्नानाविधैश्चैव चित्रितायां सुशोभनैः
नानारत्नमये पीठे कल्पयित्वा यथाविधि |
किरीटेन ततः पश्चाद्वसिष्ठेन महात्मना
ऋत्विग्भिर्भूषणैश्चैव समयोक्ष्यत राघवः |
verses.iast:
brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ pūrvaṃ kirīṭaṃ ratnaśobhitam
abhiṣiktaḥ purā yena manustaṃ dīptatejasam |
tasyānvavāye rājānaḥ kramādyenābhiṣecitāḥ
sabhāyāṃ hemakluptāyāṃ śobhitāyāṃ mahādhanaiḥ |
ratnairnānāvidhaiścaiva citritāyāṃ suśobhanaiḥ
nānāratnamaye pīṭhe kalpayitvā yathāvidhi |
kirīṭena tataḥ paścādvasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
ṛtvigbhirbhūṣaṇaiścaiva samayokṣyata rāghavaḥ |
verses.translation: With which crown, long ago, Manu the emperor was adorned while he was consecrated and with which, the kings followed in his line were successively adorned while they were coronated, that crown studded with precious jewels, fashioned by Brahma at the beginning of creation and dazzling with splendour, being kept according to practice on a throne adorned with many kinds of precious stones in the council-hall, studded with gold, graced with abundant riches, decorated and shiningly made with most charming jewels of various kinds, and thereafter Rama duly adorned by that crown as well as jewels by the great-souled Vasishta and other priests officiating at the coronation-ceremony.

glosses.meaning: was adorned when he was coronated
the kings who followed in his line
were successively adorned when they were coronated
adorned with many kinds of precious stones
and other priests officiating at the coronation-ceremony.

verses.devanagari:
छत्रं तस्य च जग्राह शत्रुघ्नः पाण्डुरन् शुभम्
श्वेतन् च वालव्यजनन् सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः |
अपरन् चन्द्रसङ्काशन् राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः
verses.iast:
chatraṃ tasya ca jagrāha śatrughnaḥ pāṇḍuran śubham
śvetan ca vAlavyajanan sugrIvo vAnareśvaraḥ |
aparan candrasañkAśan rAkṣasendro vibhIṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Shatrughna held over him, a white and charming parasol; Sugreeva the king of monkeys, a white whisk and vibhishana the lord of demons, another whisk shining like the moon.

verses.devanagari:
मालान् ज्वलन्तीन् वपुषा काञ्चनीं शतपुष्कराम् |
राघवाय ददौ वायुर्वासवेन प्रचोदितः
verses.iast:
mAlAn jvalantIn vapuṣA kAñcanIṃ śatapuṣkarAm |
rAghavAya dadau vAyurvAsavena pracoditaḥ
verses.translation: Encouraged by Indra, the lord of celestials, the wind-god presented to Rama, a golden garland consisting of a hundred lotuses and which looked shining brilliantly.

glosses.meaning: by Indra the lord of celestials

verses.devanagari:
सर्वरत्नसमायुक्तं मणिरत्नविभूषितम् |
मुक्ताहारं नरेन्द्राय ददौ शक्रप्रचोदितः
verses.iast:
sarvaratnasamAyuktaṃ maṇiratnavibhUṣitam |
muktAhAraṃ narendrAya dadau śakrapracoditaḥ
verses.translation: Induced by Indra, the wind-god presented to Rama the king, a chain of pearls, adorned with gems and endowed with several types of precious stones.

glosses.meaning: and endowed with several types of precious stones.

verses.devanagari:
प्रजगुर्देवगन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरो गणाः |
अभिषेके तदर्हस्य तदा रामस्य धीमतः
verses.iast:
prajagurdevagandharvA nanṛtuścApsaro gaṇAḥ |
abhiṣeke tadarhasya tadA rAmasya dhImataḥ
verses.translation: On that occasion of the coronation-ceremony of the intelligent Rama, who was well-deserving it, the celestial-musicians among the celestials gracefully sang and troupes of Apsaras (celestial nymphs) danced.

glosses.meaning: at that time of coronation-ceremony of intelligent Rama
the celestial musicians among the celestials

verses.devanagari:
भूमिः सस्यवती चैव फलवन्तश्च पादपाः |
गन्धवन्ति च पुष्पाणि बभूवू राघवोत्सवे
verses.iast:
bhUmiḥ sasyavatI caiva phalavantaśca pAdapAḥ |
gandhavanti ca puṣpAṇi babhUvU rAghavotsave
verses.translation: On the occasion of that merriment of coronation to Rama, the earth was bearing a rich crop, the trees were laden with fruits and fragrant flowers.

glosses.meaning: on the occasion of that merriment (of coronation) to Rama
was bearing a rich crop paadapaaH = the trees

verses.devanagari:
सहस्रशतमश्वानान् धेनूनां च गवां तथा |
ददौ शतन् वृषान्पूर्वन् द्विजेभ्यो मनुजर्षभः
verses.iast:
sahasraśatamaśvAnAn dhenUnAṃ ca gavAṃ tathA |
dadau śatan vṛṣAnpUrvan dvijebhyo manujarṣabhaḥ
verses.translation: Rama the foremost among men, first gave away to Brahmanas, a hundred thousand horses and cows that have lately calved as well as a hundred bulls.

verses.devanagari:
त्रिंशत्कोटीर्हिरण्यस्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुनः |
नानाभरणवस्त्राणि महार्हाणि च राघवः
verses.iast:
triṃśatkoṭIrhiraṇyasya brAhmaṇebhyo dadau punaḥ |
nAnAbharaṇavastrAṇi mahArhAṇi ca rAghavaḥ
verses.translation: Rama again gave to Brahmanas, thirty crores of gold coins, all kinds of very costly jewels and raiment.

verses.devanagari:
अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशान् काञ्चनीं मणिविग्रहाम् |
सुग्रीवाय स्रजन् दिव्यां प्रायच्छन्मनुजर्षभः
verses.iast:
arkaraśmipratIkAśAn kAñcanIṃ maṇivigrahAm |
sugrIvAya srajan divyAṃ prAyacchanmanujarṣabhaḥ
verses.translation: Rama gave to Sugreeva, a beautiful chaplet, studded with plenty of gems, looking like a beam of sun-light.

glosses.meaning: looking like a beam of sun-light.

verses.devanagari:
वैदूर्यमणिचित्रे च वज्ररत्नविभूषिते |
वालिपुत्राय धृतिमानङ्गदायाङ्गदे ददौ
verses.iast:
vaidUryamaṇicitre ca vajraratnavibhUṣite |
vAliputrAya dhṛtimAnañgadAyAñgade dadau
verses.translation: The joyful Rama presented to Angada, the son of Vali, a bracelet worn on upper arm, conspicuously studded with cat's eye gems and adorned with jewels and gems.

glosses.meaning: a bracelet worn on upper arm
conspicuously studded with cat's eye gems
and adorned with jewels and gems.

verses.devanagari:
मणिप्रवरजुष्टन् च मुक्ताहारमनुत्तमम् |
सीतायै प्रददौ रामश्चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभम्
अरजे वाससी दिव्ये शुभान्याभरणानि च |
verses.iast:
maṇipravarajuṣṭan ca muktAhAramanuttamam |
sItAyai pradadau rAmaścandraraśmisamaprabham
araje vAsasI divye śubhAnyAbharaṇAni ca |
verses.translation: Rama presented to Seetha, an excellent string of pearls, furnished with superior gems, shining like a beam of moon-light; two clean and beautiful raiment and lovely ornaments.

glosses.meaning: shining like that beam of moon-light

verses.devanagari:
अवेक्षमाणा वैदेही प्रददौ वायुसूनवे
अवमुच्यात्मनः कण्ठाद्धारन् जनकनन्दिनी |
अवैक्षत हरीन्सर्वान्भर्तारन् च मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.iast:
avekṣamAṇA vaidehI pradadau vAyusUnave
avamucyAtmanaḥ kaṇṭhAddhAran janakanandinI |
avaikṣata harInsarvAnbhartAran ca muhurmuhuḥ
verses.translation: Looking towards Hanuma the monkey, Seetha, daughter of Janaka, having taken off the pearl-string from her neck, repeatedly caught the glimpse of all the monkeys and her husband.

verses.devanagari:
तामिङ्गितज्ञः सम्प्रेक्ष्य बभाषे जनकात्मजाम् |
प्रदेहि सुभगे हारन् यस्य तुष्टासि भामिनि
तेजो धृतिर्यशो दाक्ष्यं सामर्थ्यं विनयो नयः |
पौरुषन् विक्रमो बुद्धिर्यस्मिन्नेतानि नित्यदा
verses.iast:
tAmiñgitaGYaḥ samprekṣya babhAṣe janakAtmajAm |
pradehi subhage hAran yasya tuṣṭAsi bhAmini
tejo dhṛtiryaśo dākṣyaṃ sāmarthyaṃ vinayo nayaḥ |
pauruṣan vikramo buddhiryasminnetAni nityadA
verses.translation: Looking at her, Rama who was acquainted with the gesture of another spoke to Seetha as follows: "Dear Seetha! Give the pearl-necklace to a person, with whom you are pleased and in whom the following viz. sharpness, firmness, renown, dexterity, competence, modesty, prudence, virility, prowess and intelligence are ever present."

glosses.meaning: to that Seetha (as follows): subhage bhaamini = O dear Seetha

verses.devanagari:
ददौ सा वायुपुत्राय तन् हारमसितेक्षणा |
हनूमान्स्तेन हारेण शुशुभे वानरर्षभः
चन्द्रांशुचयगौरेण श्वेताभ्रेण यथाचलः |
verses.iast:
dadau sA vAyuputrAya tan hAramasitekṣaṇA |
hanUmAnstena hAreṇa śuśubhe vAnararṣabhaḥ
candrAṃśucayagaureṇa śvetAbhreṇa yathAcalaḥ |
verses.translation: The black-eyed Seetha gave that pearl necklace to Hanuma. Hanuma, the foremost among the monkeys, by wearing that necklace, which was as white as a heap of moonlight-beams, shone brilliantly as a mountain silvered by a white cloud.

glosses.meaning: which was white as a heap of beams of moonlight

verses.devanagari:
सर्वे वानरवृद्धाश्च ये चान्ये वानरोत्तमाः
वासोभिर्भूषणैश्चैव यथार्हं प्रतिपूजिताः |
verses.iast:
sarve vānaravṛddhāśca ye cānye vānarottamāḥ
vāsobhirbhūṣaṇaiścaiva yathārhaṃ pratipūjitāḥ |
verses.translation: All the elder ones among the monkeys and others, who were foremost among the moneys, were honoured suitably with raiment and ornaments.

glosses.meaning: all the elder ones among the monkeys

verses.devanagari:
ततो द्विविद मैन्दाभ्यां नीलाय च परन्तपः
सर्वान्कामगुणान्वीक्ष्य प्रददौ वसुधाधिपः |
verses.iast:
tato dvivida maindAbhyAṃ nIlAya ca parantapaḥ
sarvAnkAmaguṇAnvIkṣya pradadau vasudhAdhipaḥ |
verses.translation: Thereafter, Rama the tormentator of enemies, having thought over, presented articles according to their inclinations, to Mainada, Dvivida and Nila.

verses.devanagari:
विभीषणोऽथ सुग्रीवो हनुमान् जाम्बवांस्तथा
सर्ववानरवृद्धाश्च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा |
यथार्हं पूजिताः सर्वे कामै रत्नैश्च पुष्कलैर्
प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे जग्मुरेव यथागतम् |
verses.iast:
vibhīṣaṇo'tha sugrīvo hanumān jāmbavāṃstathā
sarvavAnaravṛddhAśca rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā |
yathArhaṃ pUjitAḥ sarve kAmai ratnaiśca puṣkalair
prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve jagmureva yathAgatam |
verses.translation: Rama, who was unwearied in action, then suitably honoured Vibhishana, Sugreeva, Hanuma, Jamabavan and all other eminent monkeys with desired objects and abundant gifts. All of them went back, delighted in mind even as they had come.

verses.devanagari:
नत्वा सर्वे महात्मानस्ततस्ते वानरर्षभाः
विसृष्टाः पार्थिवेन्द्रेण किष्किन्धां समुपागमन् |
verses.iast:
natvā sarve mahātmānastataste vānararṣabhāḥ
visṛṣṭāḥ pārthivendreṇa kiṣkindhāṃ samupāgaman |
verses.translation: Thereafter, all those excellent great souled monkeys, offering their salutation to Rama and getting permission from him, returned to Kishkindha.

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवो वानरश्रेष्ठो दृष्ट्वा रामाभिषेचनम्
पूजितश्चैव रामेण किष्किन्धां प्राविशत्पुरीम् |
verses.iast:
sugrīvo vānaraśreṣṭho dṛṣṭvā rāmābhiṣecanam
pūjitaścaiva rāmeṇa kiṣkindhāṃ prāviśatpurīm |
verses.translation: Having seen Rama's coronation-ceremony, Sugreeva the chief of monkeys, after getting honoured by Rama, entered the city of Kishkindha.

verses.devanagari:
विभीषणोऽपि ध्र्मात्मा सह रैर्नैरृतर्षभैः
लब्ध्वा कुलधनं राजा लङ्कां प्रायान् महायशाः |
verses.iast:
vibhīṣaṇo'pi dhrmātmā saha rairnairṛtarṣabhaiḥ
labdhvā kuladhanaṃ rājā laṇ^kāṃ prāyān mahāyaśāḥ |
verses.translation: The righteous and the renowned king Vibhishana too, after obtaining the treasure of his race (kingdom of demons), followed by those foremost of demons, returned to Lanka.

glosses.meaning: the treasure of the race (the kingdom of demons)

verses.devanagari:
स राज्यमखिलं शासन्निहतारिर्महायशाः
राघवः परमोदारः शशास परया मुदा |
उवाच लक्ष्मणं रामो धर्मज्ञं धर्मवत्सलः
verses.iast:
sa rājyamakhilaṃ śāsannihatārirmahāyaśāḥ
rāghavaḥ paramodāraḥ śaśāsa parayā mudā |
uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo dharmajJṇaṃ dharmavatsalaḥ
verses.translation: That renowned Rama, of a very generous nature, having destroyed his enemies and ruling the entire kingdom, enjoyed it with a great delight. Rama, affectionate of righteousness, spoke to Lakshmana, the knower of righteousness (as followers):

verses.devanagari:
आतिष्ठ धर्मज्ञ मया सहेमां |
गां पूर्वराजाध्युषितां बलेन |
तुल्यं मया त्वं पितृभिर्धृता या |
तां यौवराज्ये धुरमुद्वहस्व
verses.iast:
ātiṣṭha dharmajJṇa mayā sahemāṃ |
gāṃ pūrvarājādhyuṣitāṃ balena |
tulyaṃ mayā tvaṃ pitṛbhirdhṛtā yā |
tāṃ yauvarājye dhuramudvahasva
verses.translation: "O Lakshmana, the knower of what is right! Rule with me, this earth, as ruled by the earlier kings, with the help of an army. Installed in the office of Prince Regent, bear like me, the burden (of sovereignty), which was borne by our forefathers."

glosses.meaning: as ruled by the earlier kiings
in the office of Prince Regent

verses.devanagari:
सर्वात्मना पर्यनुनीयमानो |
यदा न सौमित्रिरुपैति योगम् |
नियुज्यमानोऽ पि च यावराज्ये
ततोऽभ्यषिञ्चद्भरतं महात्मा
verses.iast:
sarvātmanā paryanunīyamāno |
yadā na saumitrirupaiti yogam |
niyujyamāno' pi ca yāvarājye
tato'bhyaṣiJṇcadbharataṃ mahātmā
verses.translation: When Lakshmana did not give his consent, even though being repeatedly entreated in all ways, nay even being appointed to the office of Prince Regent, the great-souled Rama thereupon consecrated Bharata.

glosses.meaning: to the office of prince Regent

verses.devanagari:
पौण्डरीकाश्वमेधाभ्यान् वाजपेयेन चासकृत् |
अन्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैरयजत्पार्थिवर्षभः
verses.iast:
pauṇḍarIkAśvamedhAbhyAn vAjapeyena cAsakṛt |
anyaiśca vividhairyaGYairayajatpArthivarṣabhaḥ
verses.translation: Rama propitiated the gods by performing Paundarika, Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and other sacrifices many times.

verses.devanagari:
राज्यन् दशसहस्राणि प्राप्य वर्षाणि राघवः |
शताश्वमेधानाजह्रे सदश्वान्भूरिदक्षिणान्
verses.iast:
rAjyan daśasahasrAṇi prApya varṣAṇi rAghavaḥ |
śatAśvamedhAnAjahre sadaśvAnbhUridakṣiṇAn
verses.translation: Having enjoyed the kingship for ten thousand years, Rama performed a hundred horse-sacrifices, in which good horses were sacrificed and numerous gifts bestowed.

glosses.meaning: in which good horses were sacrificed
and in which numerous gifts were bestowed.

verses.devanagari:
आजानुलम्बिबाहुश्च महास्कन्धः प्रतापवान् |
लक्ष्मणानुचरो रामः पृथिवीमन्वपालयत्
verses.iast:
AjAnulambibAhuśca mahAskandhaḥ pratApavAn |
lakṣmaṇAnucaro rAmaḥ pṛthivImanvapAlayat
verses.translation: That Rama, having his long arms reaching down his knees, having a broad chest and glorious, ruled this earth with Lakshmana as his companion.

glosses.meaning: having long arms reaching down to his knees

verses.devanagari:
राघवश्चापि धर्मात्मा प्राप्य राज्यमनुत्तमम् |
ईजे बहुविधैर्यज्ञैः ससुतभ्रातृबान्धवः
verses.iast:
rāghavaścāpi dharmātmā prāpya rājyamanuttamam |
īje bahuvidhairyajJṇaiḥ sasutabhrātṛbāndhavaḥ
verses.translation: Obtaining a very great kingdom the righteous Rama propitiated the almighty with many kinds of sacrifices, with the team-work of his sons, brothers and relatives.

glosses.meaning: with the co-operation of his sons

verses.devanagari:
न पर्यदेवन्विधवा न च व्यालकृतं भयम् |
न व्याधिजं भयन् वापि रामे राज्यं प्रशासति
verses.iast:
na paryadevanvidhavA na ca vyAlakṛtaṃ bhayam |
na vyAdhijaṃ bhayan vApi rAme rAjyaṃ praśAsati
verses.translation: While Rama was ruling the kingdom, there were no widows to lament, nor there was no danger from wild animals, nor any fear born of diseases.

glosses.meaning: there were no widows to lament

verses.devanagari:
निर्दस्युरभवल्लोको नानर्थः कन् चिदस्पृशत् |
न च स्म वृद्धा बालानां प्रेतकार्याणि कुर्वते
verses.iast:
nirdasyurabhavalloko nAnarthaḥ kan cidaspṛśat |
na ca sma vṛddhA bAlAnAṃ pretakAryAṇi kurvate
verses.translation: The world was bereft of thieves and robberies. No one felt worthless nor did old people perform obsequies concerning youngsters.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वं मुदितमेवासीत्सर्वो धर्मपरोअभवत् |
राममेवानुपश्यन्तो नाभ्यहिन्सन्परस्परम्
verses.iast:
sarvaṃ muditamevAsItsarvo dharmaparoabhavat |
rAmamevAnupaśyanto nAbhyahinsanparasparam
verses.translation: Every creature felt pleased. Every one was intent on virtue. Turning their eyes towards Rama alone, creatures did not kill one another.

verses.devanagari:
आसन्वर्षसहस्राणि तथा पुत्रसहस्रिणः |
निरामया विशोकाश्च रामे राज्यं प्रशासति
verses.iast:
AsanvarṣasahasrAṇi tathA putrasahasriṇaḥ |
nirAmayA viśokAśca rAme rAjyaṃ praśAsati
verses.translation: While Rama was ruling the kingdom, people survived for thousands of years, with thousands of their progeny, all free of illness and grief.

verses.devanagari:
रामो रामो राम इति प्रजानामभवन् कथाः |
रामभूतं जगाभूद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति
verses.iast:
rāmo rāmo rāma iti prajānāmabhavan kathāḥ |
rāmabhūtaṃ jagābhūdrāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
verses.translation: While Rama ruled the kingdom, the talks of the people centered round Rama, Rama and Rama. The world became Rama's world.

verses.devanagari:
नित्यपुष्पा नित्यफलास्तरवः स्कन्धविस्तृताः |
कालवर्षी च पर्जन्यः सुखस्पर्शश्च मारुतः
verses.iast:
nityapuṣpA nityaphalAstaravaḥ skandhavistṛtAḥ |
kAlavarṣI ca parjanyaḥ sukhasparśaśca mArutaḥ
verses.translation: The trees there were bearing flowers and fruits regularly, without any injury by pests and insects. The clouds were raining in time and the wind was delightful to the touch.

verses.devanagari:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा लोभविवर्जिताः |
स्वकर्मसु प्रवर्तन्ते तुष्ठाः स्वैरेव कर्मभिः
आसन् प्रजा धर्मपरा रामे शासति नानृताः |
verses.iast:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā lobhavivarjitāḥ |
svakarmasu pravartante tuṣṭhAḥ svaireva karmabhiḥ
Asan prajA dharmaparA rAme śAsati nAnṛtAḥ |
verses.translation: Brahmins (the priest-class), Kshatriyas (the warrior-class), Vaishyas (the class of merchants and agriculturists), Shudras (the servant-class) were performing their own duties, satisfied with their own work and bereft of any greed. While Rama was ruling, the people were intent on virtue and lived without telling lies.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वे लक्षणसम्पन्नाः सर्वे धर्मपरायणाः
दशवर्षसहस्राणि रामो राज्यमकारयत् |
verses.iast:
sarve lakṣaṇasampannAḥ sarve dharmaparAyaṇAḥ
daśavarṣasahasrAṇi rAmo rAjyamakArayat |
verses.translation: All the people were endowed with excellent characteristics. All were engaged in virtue. Rama was engaged in the kingship thus for one thousand years.

verses.devanagari:
धर्मयं यशस्यमायुष्यं राज्ञां च विजाअवहम्
आदिकाव्यमिदं चार्षं पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम् |
पठेद्यः शृणुयाल्लोके नरः पापात्प्रमुच्यते
verses.iast:
dharmayaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ rājJṇāṃ ca vijāavaham
ādikāvyamidaṃ cārṣaṃ purā vālmīkinā kṛtam |
paṭhedyaḥ śṛṇuyālloke naraḥ pāpātpramucyate
verses.translation: In this world, whoever person reads and listens to this foremost lyric derived from the speech of a sage, which is endowed with righteousness, conferring fame and longevity, fetching victory to kings and as written at first by Valmiki, that person is delivered from all misfortune.

glosses.meaning: and a lyric derived from the speech of a sage

verses.devanagari:
पुत्रकामश्च पुत्रान्वै धनकामो धनानि च |
लभते मनुजो लोके श्रुत्वा रामाभिषेचनम्
महीं विजयते राजा रिपूंश्चाप्यधितिष्ठति |
verses.iast:
putrakāmaśca putrānvai dhanakāmo dhanāni ca |
labhate manujo loke śrutvā rāmābhiṣecanam
mahīṃ vijayate rājā ripūṃścāpyadhitiṣṭhati |
verses.translation: On hearing the narrative of his coronation in this world, a person seeking for sons gets sons. A person looking for wealth, gets the riches. A king conquers the earth and overcomes his enemies.

glosses.meaning: and a person looking for wealth

verses.devanagari:
राघवेण यथा माता सुमित्रा लक्ष्मणेन च
भरतेन च कैकेयी जिवपुत्रास्तथा स्त्रियः |
भविष्यन्ति सदानन्दाः पुत्रपौत्रसमन्विताः
verses.iast:
rāghaveṇa yathā mātā sumitrā lakṣmaṇena ca
bharatena ca kaikeyī jivaputrāstathā striyaḥ |
bhaviṣyanti sadānandāḥ putrapautrasamanvitāḥ
verses.translation: Even as Kausalya, the mother has Rama as her living son, or as Sumitra has Lakshmana or as Kaikeyi has Bharata, the women likewise can become mothers of living sons, endowed with children as well as grand children and thus become happy forever.

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा रामायणमिदं दीर्घमायिश्च विन्दति |
रामस्य विजयं चैव सर्वमक्लिष्ठकर्मणः
verses.iast:
śrutvā rāmāyaṇamidaṃ dīrghamāyiśca vindati |
rāmasya vijayaṃ caiva sarvamakliṣṭhakarmaṇaḥ
verses.translation: On hearing this epic of Ramayana and all the episode of victory of Rama, who was unweary in his actions, a person gets longevity to life.

glosses.meaning: who was unweary in his actions

verses.devanagari:
शृणोति य इत्दं काव्यं पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम् |
श्रद्दधानो जितक्रोधो दुर्गाण्यतितरत्यसौ
verses.iast:
śṛṇoti ya itdaṃ kāvyaṃ purā vālmīkinā kṛtam |
śraddadhāno jitakrodho durgāṇyatitaratyasau
verses.translation: He or she, who hears with attention and with a subdued anger, this poetic composition done by Valmiki long ago, that person overcomes the difficulties.

verses.devanagari:
समागम्य प्रवासान्ते रमन्ते सह बान्धवैः |
शृण्वन्ति य इदं काव्यं पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम्
verses.iast:
samāgamya pravāsānte ramante saha bāndhavaiḥ |
śṛṇvanti ya idaṃ kāvyaṃ purā vālmīkinā kṛtam
verses.translation: Whoever hears this poetical composition written by Valmiki long ago, they at the conclusion of their absence from home, meet their relatives and get rejoiced.

glosses.meaning: at the conclusion of their absence from home

verses.devanagari:
ते प्रार्थितान् वरान् सर्वान् प्राप्नुवन्तीह राघवात् |
श्रवणेन सुराः सर्वे प्रीयन्ते संप्रशृण्वताम्
verses.iast:
te prārthitān varān sarvān prāpnuvantīha rāghavāt |
śravaṇena surāḥ sarve prīyante sampraśṛṇvatām
verses.translation: They get all the boons, entreated from Rama. All the gods get pleased with those who carefully listen to it.

glosses.meaning: with those who carefully listen to it.

verses.devanagari:
विनायकाश्च शाम्यन्ति गृहे तिष्ठन्ति यस्य वै |
विजयेत महीं राजा प्रवासि स्वस्तिमान् भवेत्
verses.iast:
vināyakāśca śāmyanti gṛhe tiṣṭhanti yasya vai |
vijayeta mahīṃ rājā pravāsi svastimān bhavet
verses.translation: Whoever carefully listens to the epic in his house, all obstacles come to an end. A king conquers the earth. A person staying away from home, fares well.

glosses.meaning: a person absenting away from home

verses.devanagari:
स्त्रियो रजस्वलाः श्रुत्वा पुत्रान् सूयुरनुत्तमान् |
पूजयंश्च पठंश्चनमितिहासं पुरातनम्
verses.iast:
striyo rajasvalāḥ śrutvā putrān sūyuranuttamān |
pūjayaṃśca paṭhaṃścanamitihāsaṃ purātanam
verses.translation: On hearing the epic, the menstruating women give birth to excellent sons. The adorer and the reader of this ancient epic gets relieved of all sins and obtains longer life.

glosses.meaning: of all sins avaapnuyaat = and gets

verses.devanagari:
प्रणम्य शिरसा नित्यं श्रोतव्यं क्षत्रियैर्द्विजात्
ऐश्वर्यं पुत्रलाभश्च भविष्यति न संशयः |
रामायणमिदं कृत्स्नं शृण्वतः पठतः सदा
verses.iast:
praṇamya śirasā nityaṃ śrotavyaṃ kṣatriyairdvijāt
aiśvaryaṃ putralābhaśca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ |
rāmāyaṇamidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śṛṇvataḥ paṭhataḥ sadā
verses.translation: The epic is to be listened by warrior-class, after offering their salutation with their heads bent low, from brahmins every day regularly. There is no doubt that the listener and the reader of this entire Ramayana will get lordship and the birth of a son.

glosses.meaning: it is to be listened to
and the birth of a son.

verses.devanagari:
प्रीयते सततं रामः सहि मिष्णुः सनातनः |
आदिदेवो महाबाहुर्हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः
साक्षाद्रामो रघुश्रेष्ठः शेषो लक्ष्मण उच्यते |
verses.iast:
prīyate satataṃ rāmaḥ sahi miṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ |
ādidevo mahābāhurharirnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
sākṣādrāmo raghuśreṣṭhaḥ śeṣo lakṣmaṇa ucyate |
verses.translation: Rama gets forever pleased with him who listens to or reads Ramayana daily. He is indeed the eternal Vishnu, the Lord of preservation. Rama is the primordial Lord, clearly placed before the eyes the powerful Lord removing the sins and the great-armed, who has abode on waters (of the ocean of milk) Sesha (the serpent-god forming his couch is said to be Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: is indeed the eternal Vishnu the Lord of preservation
clearly placed before tlp[- = he eyes
who has abode on the waters (of the ocean of milk)

verses.devanagari:
एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तमाख्यानं भद्रमस्तु वः
प्रव्याहरत विस्रब्धं बलं विष्णोः प्रवर्धताम् |
verses.iast:
evametatpurāvṛttamākhyānaṃ bhadramastu vaḥ
pravyāharata visrabdhaṃ balaṃ viṣṇoḥ pravardhatām |
verses.translation: Tell this epic which occurred long ago in this manner, to those who ask for it, fearlessly. Let there be happiness to you! Let the strength of Vishnu increase!

glosses.meaning: let there be happiness to you!
let the strength of Vishnu increase!.

verses.devanagari:
देवाश्च सर्वे तुष्यन्ति ग्रहणाच्छ्रवणात्तथा
रामायणस्य श्रवणे तुष्यन्ति पितरः सदा |
verses.iast:
devāśca sarve tuṣyanti grahaṇācchravaṇāttathā
rāmāyaṇasya śravaṇe tuṣyanti pitaraḥ sadā |
verses.translation: By studying and listening to this epic, all the gods get appeased. By listening to this Ramayana, the forefathers forever get pleased.

verses.devanagari:
भक्त्या रामस्य ये चेमां संहितामृषिणा कृताम्
ये लिखन्तीह च नरास्तेषां वासस्त्रिविष्टपे |
verses.iast:
bhaktyā rāmasya ye cemāṃ saṃhitāmṛṣiṇā kṛtām
ye likhantīha ca narāsteṣāṃ vāsastriviṣṭape |
verses.translation: To those persons who transcribe with devotion this collection of poems depicting the story of Rama residence in heaven is assured.

verses.devanagari:
कुटुम्बवृद्धिं धनधान्यवृद्धिं |
स्त्रियश्च मुख्याह् सुखमुत्तमं च |
श्रुत्वा शुभं काव्यमिदं महार्थं |
प्राप्नोति सर्वां भुवि चार्थसिद्धिम्
verses.iast:
kuṭumbavṛddhiṃ dhanadhānyavṛddhiṃ |
striyaśca mukhyāh sukhamuttamaṃ ca |
śrutvā śubhaṃ kāvyamidaṃ mahārthaṃ |
prāpnoti sarvāṃ bhuvi cārthasiddhim
verses.translation: By listening to this highly meaningful and auspicious poetical composition, a person gets family-prosperity, augmentation in money and grain, superior women, exquisite happiness and all the acquisition of wealth on this earth.

verses.devanagari:
आयुष्यमारोग्यकरं यशस्यं |
सौभ्रातृकं बुद्धिकरं शुभं च |
श्रोतव्यमेतन्नियमेन सद्भि |
राख्यानमोजस्करमृद्धिकामैः
verses.iast:
āyuṣyamārogyakaraṃ yaśasyaṃ |
saubhrātṛkaṃ buddhikaraṃ śubhaṃ ca |
śrotavyametanniyamena sadbhi |
rākhyānamojaskaramṛddhikāmaiḥ
verses.translation: This narrative is to be listened invariably by good people, seeking for wisdom, longevity, health, fame, fraternity, intelligence, welfare and brilliance.

glosses.meaning: by good people seeking for wisdom
